title: The Arcadia Formation: infrastructure, governance, land, and the station
dek: A sequenced public-record packet showing how infrastructure, planning, assessment governance, ownership, and project-specific approvals line up in downtown Arcadia. The report makes the formation visible without generating a master-plan, coordination, benefit, or wrongdoing conclusion.

history.change: Initial structured reporter report compiled from the receipted Arcadia field-autopsy case and its candidate-only evidence trails.

records_target.text: The stronger formation theory turns on six record classes: recorder deed images and the pre-2016 ownership chain; DAIA enabling, renewal, assessment, and authorization records; executed station betterment and funding agreements; public-land disposition files; project-specific support and applicant-control records; and financing source-and-use records.
records_target.qualification: This is a reporting roadmap. Missing records are not evidence that a master plan, coordinated control, benefit, or wrongdoing existed.

matrix.empty_state_label: No case-specific connection is established in the opened record.

controls.title: Comparable corridors show public planning and parcel assembly without shared Arcadia actors
Policy, land economics, anticipation, and lawful growth coalitions are ordinary mechanisms

workplan.title: Recover the deed chain before interpreting ownership concentration
workplan.date_window: Pre-2016 ownership through the 2024-2025 parcel transactions
custodians: Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk and Assessor
Named grantors, grantees, title insurers, lenders, and project entities
records: Recorder deed images, document indexes, transfer declarations, options, and assignments
Parcel maps, predecessor APN chains, title reports, lender instruments, and beneficial-ownership records
routes: Recorder document orders and Assessor parcel histories
workplan.decision_test: Establish who held which parcel, under what legal entity, and when; shared addresses, agents, or later transactions cannot substitute for the deed chain.

workplan.title: Recover the assessment district's enabling and authorization records
workplan.date_window: CBD initiation in 2012 through current assessment and project-advocacy activity
custodians: Arcadia City Clerk, City Manager, Finance, and Successor Agency
Downtown Arcadia Improvement Association and assessed property owners
records: Petition, enabling resolution, engineer's report, assessment roll, bylaws, and renewal instruments
Agendas, minutes, support letters, authorizations, votes, recusals, budgets, and city oversight records
routes: California Public Records Act requests and City Clerk archives
workplan.decision_test: Separate formation and routine assessment governance from any project-specific support, authorization, conflict control, or influence.

workplan.title: Reconcile the station cost share and every local betterment
workplan.date_window: Measure R approval through station opening and close-out
custodians: Foothill Gold Line Construction Authority and Los Angeles Metro
City of Arcadia finance, engineering, public works, and clerk offices
records: Executed betterment, funding, grade-separation, parking, and pedestrian-linkage agreements
Board approvals, change orders, invoices, close-out reports, land contributions, and maintenance obligations
routes: Construction Authority and Metro board archives
City capital budgets and records requests
Bond, grant, and interagency agreement files
workplan.decision_test: Keep the core regional extension, grade separation, station betterments, parking, pedestrian linkage, and maintenance as separate scopes and amounts.

workplan.title: Resolve who authorized project-specific advocacy and participation
workplan.date_window: DAIA officer and applicant roles from 2021 through the 2025 Town Center decision
custodians: DAIA officers, board members, counsel, and records custodian
City planning staff, commissioners, applicants, property owners, and named intermediaries
records: Officer schedules, statements of information, board rosters, agendas, minutes, and attendance
The Town Center support letter, authorization trail, communications, votes, recusals, and conflict advice
routes: Claim-ID-keyed on-record questions to named participants
workplan.decision_test: Role overlap is a reporting lead only; establish or defeat a project-specific act, authorization, vote, communication, or conflict control.

workplan.title: Inventory public land, easements, and disposition decisions
workplan.date_window: Redevelopment acquisition through successor-agency disposition and current downtown ownership
custodians: Arcadia Successor Agency, City Clerk, Finance, and Public Works
Los Angeles County oversight, assessor, and recorder offices
records: Long-range property management plans, deeds, leases, disposition agreements, easements, and parking inventories
Successor-agency approvals, appraisals, bids, development covenants, and present parcel status
workplan.decision_test: Distinguish actual public acquisition, contribution, lease, sale, or easement from area-wide infrastructure and planning that increased private development capacity.

workplan.title: Trace financing sources and uses without inferring misconduct
workplan.date_window: Project capitalization, acquisition, construction, refinancing, and any distress event
custodians: Project entities, lenders, investors, regional centers, and finance counterparties
City planning, building, and economic-development offices
records: Capital stacks, loan and equity instruments, offering records, NCE/JCE identities, and source-and-use schedules
Acquisition consideration, construction draws, subsidies, guarantees, refinancing, and repayment records
routes: Federal, state, court, and offering records
workplan.decision_test: Identify the actual source and use of funds while keeping EB-5 participation, project distress, ownership, and wrongdoing as separate questions.

workplan.title: Build same-line and different-corridor controls before interpreting convergence
workplan.date_window: Planning announcement through station opening, parcel assembly, assessment governance, and development delivery
custodians: Monrovia, Duarte, Pasadena, Azusa, Los Angeles, and transit-agency records offices
Comparable BIDs, developers, and parcel owners
records: Specific plans, public improvements, parcel acquisitions, developer agreements, entitlements, and delivery outcomes
BID or PBID enabling instruments, boundaries, assessments, governance, and project-specific advocacy
routes: Comparable developer, district, and community sourcing
workplan.decision_test: Determine which Arcadia features are ordinary corridor formation, which are uncommon, and which remain unmeasured rather than treating recurrence as coordination.

workplan.title: Separate documented market practice from policy, control, and causation
workplan.date_window: Documented residential and project-market practices through the selected downtown developments
custodians: Project designers, applicants, brokers, buyers, and public records offices
Researchers and journalists holding the cited comparable-market evidence
records: Source-explicit statements about siting, address changes, design, date selection, or marketing
Project-specific applications and communications, with a neutral denominator of nonmatching projects
routes: On-record interviews and archived public statements
Municipal address, planning, and project files
workplan.decision_test: A documented market preference or cultural practice does not establish city policy, shared ethnic action, supernatural mechanism, project control, or causal coordination.

translations.question: Which public agency acquired or improved which property, using which revenue stream, before dissolution?
Which ordinance changed allowable height, density, uses, or parking, and which parcels or applications received the benefit?
Who was assessed, who governed the proceeds, what services were authorized, and how was any project-specific position approved?
Which local improvement exceeded the regional baseline, who requested it, who paid, and who owns or maintains it?
Does the record establish a dated parcel event only, or does the deed image identify the grantor, grantee, interest, and consideration?
Which affordable-housing commitment authorized which additional units, concessions, waivers, or parking reduction?
What transfer event does the tax field indicate, and what party, interest, or beneficial owner remains unresolved without the deed?
What public land, right, funding, or approval entered the transaction, and what did the private counterparty commit to deliver?
